newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arthuis repeats supports independent central bank.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis repeats supports independent central bank.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis repeated on Monday that he supported the independence of the future European Central Bank.

He said there was no dispute over France's proposal for a special "stability council" to co-ordinate economic policies among members of European monetary union after the launch of the single currency in January 1999.
The proposal has come under fire from the German Bundesbank, which fears the council could be used to undermine the independence of the European central bank.

"There is no dispute," Arthuis told Reuters Financial Television. "We want a credible currency...I support an independent central bank. It is the case in France right now, it will be the case in the European Union," he said.
He told reporters earlier that the proposal was gathering agreement among France's European Union partners, although he said it was not discussed by EU finance ministers earlier on Monday.
He also said he welcomed the dollar's recent rise, but declined to comment on whether he expected it to climb further.
"It's better than the previous rate. The market will determine the right exchange rate," he said.
